front: Give three examples of specular reflectors in the heart.
back: Chamber walls, valve leaflets, pericardium, diaphragm — large (> λ), smooth surfaces that produce strong reflections.

front: Give two examples of non-specular reflectors (scatterers) and their significance.
back: Red blood cells and soft tissue — small or rough. They scatter US in multiple directions; scattering off RBCs is the physical basis of Doppler.

front: Under what geometric condition does refraction NOT occur at an interface?
back: When the beam is at normal incidence (90°) to the interface — no oblique component to refract.

front: How does higher transducer frequency affect scattering?
back: Higher frequency = more scatter (scatter cross-section increases with frequency). This is why high-frequency imaging shows more speckle.
